open_obligations: Check that EAS reduces to something like Khan et al.'s Elo for debate.
Note that EAS depends on the agent's propensity q to argue each answer.
Check whether EAS needs ground truth to split p_true and p_false, unlike Khan et al.'s label-free metric.
out.other_title: Persuasiveness: an unsupervised debater-strength metric based on judge approval
out.rationale: Khan et al. introduce persuasiveness, measured by judge approval (win rate and Elo) without ground-truth labels, to study debate scaling. Sudhir et al. state they generalise the debater Elo used in earlier debate experiments to any protocol with Expected Agent Score, EAS = (log p_true, log p_false) dotted with q, as a pure capability measure.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: label-free measures of agent strength for studying how oversight protocols scale with capability

text: The authors note that ASD measured on current models estimates a protocol's present training signal, and to ask whether it will hold as capabilities grow they generalize the debater Elo used in earlier debate experiments to any protocol by defining Expected Agent Score, EAS = (log p_true, log p_false) dotted with q, as a pure measure of the agent's capabilities.
title: Expected Agent Score (EAS) as a capability measure generalizing debater Elo
